I need you to investigate a customer-reported bug in the Nxeon game-hosting platform at /opt/nxeon (Next.js + Prisma + Postgres, worker at worker/index.ts handles provisioning).

Customer complaint (support ticket, customer email sasamihi35@gmail.com, running a Cobblemon Minecraft modpack server): 
- Server restarted fine per logs, but they can't connect.
- Console error says the server is running "Minecraft 26.2" (this looks like a nonsensical/impossible version string — real Minecraft versions look like "1.21.1", not "26.2" — so first figure out where that string actually comes from; it might be a mis-parsed date, a wrong version variable, or a genuinely wrong upstream default).
- Their installed mods (Cobblemon) require Minecraft 1.21.1.
- Java 25 is currently in use, but Cobblemon requires Java 21.
- They cannot find any option in the server settings UI to select or change the Minecraft version.

Your job: find the ROOT CAUSE in the actual code, not guess. Specifically:

1. Find how Minecraft server version is determined/set at provision time and at any "reinstall"/"change version" flow. Look for OsTemplate/setupScript definitions related to Minecraft/Forge/Cobblemon, and any place that picks a Minecraft version or downloads a server jar (search for strings like "1.21", "forge", "cobblemon", "MINECRAFT_VERSION", "mc_version", etc.) — likely under worker/, lib/, or a scripts/setup directory referenced by OsTemplate rows.
2. Find where "26.2" (or similar unexpected version-like string) could come from — check if it's actually a mod-loader/launcher version, a modpack version, a date-based string, or a fallback/default that's wrong. Check any auto-update logic that might pull "latest" instead of a pinned version.
3. Find where Java version is selected for a Minecraft server container/VM (look for Java 21 vs Java 25, adoptium/temurin package names, apt install openjdk-* commands, or a Java-version variable) — figure out why Java 25 would be installed when Cobblemon (and most modern modded Minecraft) needs Java 21.
4. Check the customer-facing server settings UI (likely app/dashboard/servers/[id]/... or components/customer/...) for Minecraft-type servers — confirm whether there really is no version-selector control, and if there's a version field in the schema (Prisma) that just isn't exposed in the UI, or if the version isn't stored/configurable at all.
5. Check if this is specific to modded/Cobblemon templates vs vanilla Minecraft templates — i.e., does vanilla Minecraft have a working version selector but modded doesn't?

Report back: the exact root cause with file:line references, whether it's a config/default bug or a missing feature (no version selector), whether other customers on the same OsTemplate would hit the same issue, and a concrete recommended fix. Do NOT make any code changes — this is investigation only. Do not touch the ticket or send any customer-facing reply. Keep your report focused and under 500 words plus the key file:line citations.

content.text:
## Root cause

**The paid "minecraft" `OsTemplate.setupScript` never pins a Minecraft version, and no code path anywhere ever sets one.**

`prisma/catalog.ts:272-293` (the single OsTemplate row every Minecraft/Forge/Fabric/Cobblemon customer provisions from):
```
setupScript: "curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh && docker run -d --name mc -e EULA=TRUE -e MEMORY=2G -p 25565:25565 -p 25575:25575 -v /opt/mc:/data --restart unless-stopped itzg/minecraft-server"
```
Two things are missing: (1) no image tag (`itzg/minecraft-server` = `:latest`), (2) no `-e VERSION=...`. The upstream `itzg/docker-minecraft-server` image defaults an unset `VERSION` to `LATEST` and *re-resolves* that against Mojang's manifest **on every container start**, upgrading the installed server jar in place if a newer release exists.

- `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts:212-226` — this exact behavior is documented in the codebase's own comment thread, which states outright that Minecraft's current newest calendar release is **"26.2"** and that `VERSION=LATEST` tracks it. That confirms "26.2" is a real (if newly-adopted calendar-style) upstream MC version being auto-pulled — not a parsing bug, date string, or mod-loader version leaking into the UI.
- The **free-tier** Minecraft code path (same file) was patched for exactly this hazard: `FREEMC_PLUGIN_MC_VERSION = "26.1.2"` pins plugin-based presets away from `LATEST` specifically because brand-new MC releases break plugins/mods. **That fix was never ported to the paid game-hosting catalog** — `prisma/catalog.ts`'s minecraft template still has no pin at all.
- `worker/game-variant.ts:26-31` (`applyGameVariant`) only ever injects `-e TYPE=<loader>` (vanilla/paper/purpur/fabric/forge) from `Server.gameVariant` at provision time. It never touches or injects a `VERSION` env var — confirmed by reading the whole file.
- Because nothing pins `VERSION`, every container **restart** (systemd unit wrapping `docker run`, per `worker/index.ts:185-188`) re-triggers itzg's own "is LATEST current?" check and can silently upgrade the server — matching the customer's exact symptom: "restarted fine per logs, but they can't connect."

**Java 25 is a downstream consequence, not an independent bug.** Grep across the whole repo (`prisma/*.ts`, `worker/*.ts`, `lib/*.ts`) found zero code that selects a Java version for the minecraft OsTemplate — Java selection is entirely delegated to itzg's image, which auto-picks the JRE matching whatever `VERSION` it installs. Since `VERSION` floats to "26.2," the image bundles the newest JRE it has for that release (25) instead of the Java 21 Cobblemon (built for 1.21.1) needs.

**No version selector exists anywhere in the UI, and it's a missing feature, not a hidden field.** `lib/game-config.ts:80-183` (`MINECRAFT` `FamilySchema`) lists every customer-facing field: `gamemode, difficulty, hardcore, pvp, max-players, white-list, online-mode, view-distance, motd` — no version field. `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx:306-309` renders settings straight from `schemaFor(gameFamily)`, so there's genuinely nothing to expose. `prisma/schema.prisma:569` shows `Server.gameVariant` stores only the loader (paper/forge/fabric/...); there is no Minecraft-version column on `Server` or `OsTemplate` at all (`OsTemplate.version` at line 528 is the base-OS version, e.g. "24.04" — unrelated).

**Mod install has no version guard either.** `worker/game-mods.ts` `resolveUrl()` (~line 211-217) fetches Modrinth `versions[0]` — the newest published build for the loader — with no `game_versions` filter tying the download to the server's actual MC version, so even Cobblemon's install path can't self-correct.

## Scope

Every customer on the single shared "minecraft" `OsTemplate` (all Forge/Fabric/Paper/Vanilla orders) is exposed to the same unpinned-`VERSION`/unpinned-`:latest`-image bug — it's not Cobblemon-specific. Vanilla players mostly don't notice (nothing to be incompatible with). Modded customers (Forge/Fabric/Cobblemon, anyone requiring a specific older MC+Java combo) are the ones who break, since Forge/Fabric builds and mods lag weeks behind a brand-new MC release — exactly what the free-tier fix's own comment describes happening to EssentialsX.

## Recommended fix
1. Add `-e VERSION=<pinned>` (and an explicit itzg image tag) to the minecraft `setupScript` in `prisma/catalog.ts`, mirroring the `FREEMC_PLUGIN_MC_VERSION` pattern already proven in `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts`.
2. Add a `version` field to `MINECRAFT.fields` in `lib/game-config.ts` (or a dedicated `Server.gameVersion` column) so customers can pick/pin a version, and wire it through `applyGameConfigEnv`/`applyGameVariant` into the `VERSION` env var.
3. Add a `game_versions` filter to `worker/game-mods.ts`'s Modrinth `resolveUrl()` so mod installs match the server's actual pinned MC version instead of always grabbing the newest build.
4. Backfill: existing modded servers need their `mc` container recreated with a rollback `VERSION` (e.g. 1.21.1) once the pin lands — a restart alone won't downgrade them.
